concerns.text: Task T014 hardcodes a missing data warning threshold of '>10%' and proceeds without warning if '≤10%'. The spec (Edge Cases) explicitly defers this threshold value to '[deferred]'. This task silently relaxes the spec's requirement to defer empirical values, introducing a fixed constraint not present in the source.

Task T032 references 'SC-006' as the output label for the Proxy Validity metric. The spec's Success Criteria section only defines SC-001 through SC-005. SC-006 is an orphan identifier invented in the tasks/plan, violating the requirement that tasks must not introduce new acceptance criteria or identifiers not present in the spec.

Tasks T028 and T029 implement fallback logic (degrading to OLS) if memory constraints are exceeded. While the plan mentions this, the spec FR-005 mandates fitting 'at least three distinct spatial models'. The tasks do not explicitly state that the fallback satisfies the FR-005 requirement in a degraded state, creating a semantic risk that the FR is weakened to 'attempt to fit' rather than 'must fit'.

Task T015a requires writing 'data-model.md' to document methods for SC-007. The spec's Success Criteria section only lists SC-001 through SC-005. SC-007 is an orphan identifier not defined in the spec, violating the constraint that tasks must not invent new acceptance criteria.

Task T032a mandates fetching specific literature bounds (e.g., 'EPA UHI Review 2023'). The spec and plan do not mandate specific external sources for this data, only that literature-derived bounds be used. Hardcoding a specific report name in the task creates a fragility risk and potentially violates the 'Verified Accuracy' constitution principle if that specific report is not the canonical source or is inaccessible.
